summary: Console hourly usage spikes absent after backend partition reshard
description: Issue summary: Customer reports missing hourly usage peaks in Console usage charts for a 12-hour window after an internal partition reshard job. Impact: usage graphs under-report peak traffic and billing attribution appears lower than real ingestion. Environment: NeuroDocs dedicated tenant on prod us-east-1. First seen: 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC. Customer impact: Understated per-hour usage views and potential invoice variance for high-volume hours.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Navigate to Console > Usage > Hourly view for NeuroDocs account.
2) Set time range to 2026-03-09 22:00 -> 2026-03-10 10:00 UTC.
3) Inspect chart and raw hourly CSV export.
4) Compare to raw ingestion logs in kafka/ingest for same window.
observed_behavior: Multiple sharp traffic peaks present in raw ingest topic partitions and in the deduplicated ingest logs, but the Console hourly rollup shows flattened values (peaks missing) for hours 2026-03-10 00:00-04:00 UTC. CSV export for hourly buckets shows zeros or low counts for those buckets.
expected_behavior: Console hourly usage chart and exported hourly CSV should reflect the true per-hour token/embedding counts present in raw ingestion and billing pipeline.
logs: Examples attached in investigation notes: kafka topic offsets and ingest logs referencing message keys for tenant 'neurodocs-prod' (offsets 345678..345910). Error seen in partition-manager logs: 'Shard prune: evicted late-arriving segment for partition p-42'. No 5xx from API gateway.
investigation_notes:
2026-03-10 03:10 UTC - Support received first report from customer CS team after they noticed mismatch vs internal observability.
2026-03-10 03:40 UTC - Confirmed with ingestion team that a scheduled partition reshard job ran at 2026-03-10 01:50 UTC to compact high-cardinality tenant partitions.
Hypothesis: Reshard job pruned/merged partitions and the usage-aggregator's watermark window ignored late-arriving messages that were assigned new partition IDs, causing those events to be dropped from the hourly rollups.
Checked indexer checkpoints: shard checkpoint for p-42 jumped from offset 345600 -> 345912 during the reshard, and rollup consumer committed pre-reshard offsets; after reshard, some events landed in new partition IDs and were not reprocessed for historical buckets.
Temporary reproduction: Replaying affected raw topic range (345678..345910) into a staging rollup consumer reconstitutes the missing peaks, confirming consumer omission rather than data drop.
Cross refs: linked INT-90421 (partition-manager-reshard-telemetry) and SUP-712345 (billing-discrepancy-neurodocs).
Next steps: coordinate with platform infra to run controlled replay into staging rollup pipeline, patch rollup consumer to detect reshard events and backfill, and prepare communication to customer with ETA.
